text:
lia: Hey infra — can we provision a new GPU nodepool in us-central1-tex for a low-latency inference customer? Trying to weigh instance-family rightsizing vs node boot latency. Thoughts on a10g vs a100 vs h100 and a sensible autoscaler policy?

jordan: What are the pod profiles? realtime short-lived pods, or long running heavy batches?

lia: Mostly realtime, small batches (1-8 tokens) and tight 95th latency SLO (~120ms). Pods are short-lived (concurrency bursts from webhooks). Need nodes to be ready fast so scale-up time matters more than raw throughput.

pradeep: FWIW we measured cold node boot times in this region: a10g ~45-70s (driver + kubelet), a100 ~90-150s, h100 ~180-260s (firmware + driver init). h100 wins on throughput/latency once warm but awful for cold-start.

maria: Also remember CA + scheduler delays. If PVCs or initContainers run, add ~30-60s. Cluster-autoscaler scaleUpDelay defaults can compound things.

samir: Given that, recommendation: mixed approach — small hot pool of a10g (reserved/devoted, say 4-8 nodes) for low-latency traffic, and a larger h100 pool (spot/preemptible) for heavy long-running or batched workloads. Use taints/tolerations and podTopologies to prefer hot nodes.

lia: Sounds good. How do we wire autoscaler to prefer the hot pool first and only burst to h100 when needed?

pradeep: Use two nodepools: "gpu-hot-a10g" with min=2,max=8, and "gpu-cold-h100" with min=0,max=30. On the hot pool keep a small baseline (reserved capacity) and set pod tolerations + nodeSelector. On CA set --balance-similar-node-groups and choose expander: "price" or "least-waste" depending on config. Also lower `--readiness-gates`? (depends on build).

maria: Example CA flags we used in staging:```--scale-down-enabled=true --balance-similar-node-groups=true --expander=least-waste --scale-up-delay=10s --scale-down-delay=300s```That plus warm pool works well.

lia: Warm pool? Explain.

maria: Pre-create a tiny warm pool of empty a10g nodes (tainted) that never get drained. When CA sees pending pods, scheduler can bind to those immediately. We run a small controller to recycle warm nodes during low-usage windows so they stay healthy.

ops-bot: Quota check: requested additional GPU quota in us-central1-tex for a10g (8) and h100 (20). Request ID req-12345 opened with cloud provider, ETA 2 business days.

k8s-autoscaler-bot: Observed recent CA events: scale-up blocked due to PodTopologySpread (30s), scale-up triggered but nodes NotReady 90s due to nvidia-driver module load timeout. Log excerpt:```I0303 12:04:22.123 Scale-up: group gpu-cold-h100 size 1 -> 2 ; Node kubelet: NotReady (kernel modules initializing)```

pradeep: That kernel/driver issue is key — we can speed it by preloading vendor modules in image or using node-startup script to install drivers from a local bucket (avoid long downloads). Also set `node.kubernetes.io/not-ready` thresholds lower? careful.

samir: I'll run a quick preflight to test warm pool + driver preinstall. Need approval to bump quota request priority (ops). @ops-bot can you escalate req-12345 to P1? :pray:

ops-bot: Escalation ticket created: cloud-escalate-8910. Provider response estimated 24-48 hours now.

maria: Terraform snippet for hot pool (gke example):```resource "google_container_node_pool" "gpu_hot" { name = "gpu-hot-a10g" initial_node_count = 2 autoscaling { min_node_count = 2 max_node_count = 8 } node_config { accelerators { accelerator_count = 1 accelerator_type = "a10g" } taint { key = "gpu-hot" value = "true" effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" } metadata = { "startup-script" = file("scripts/preload-drivers.sh") } } }```Tweak startup script to mount drivers from our private bucket.

pradeep: Cost note: reserved a10g warm pool ~40% of h100 per-hour cost. Using spot for the h100 pool can cut spend but add preemption risk — fallback policy needed.

samir: I'll run perf tests (cold start P95) and post numbers here. Happy to make the nodepool PR once quota lands.

lia: Thank you all — action items: (1) samir runs preflight on warm pool + driver preload, (2) ops escalate quota (req-12345), (3) pradeep to draft CA flag changes + expander recommendation, (4) maria to prepare TF nodepool PR with startup script. If anyone else wants to be on the PR tag me.

jordan: Awesome, add a short eval harness to capture cold-start P50/P95/P99 and token-per-second throughput for each instance type so we can make data-driven choice.

lia: Will do. Closing for now — thanks :thumbsup:
